title: Bringing Forward Distribution of CDC Vouchers
what_it_is: Bringing Forward Distribution of CDC Vouchers

sections.label: CDC Vouchers and inflation support
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether it will bring CDC Voucher distribution forward and issue $100 vouchers to individuals, and says it is monitoring the situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in light of persistent high inflation rates in the last few months, whether the Ministry will consider (i) bringing the distribution of CDC Vouchers forward to the third quarter of 2022 instead of January 2023 and (ii) issuing $100 CDC Vouchers to every Singaporean aged more than 21 years old instead of to each household.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: These vouchers can be used at over 18,000 participating heartland merchants and hawkers until the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: As of September 2022, about 97% and 87% of Singaporean households have claimed their December 2021 and May 2022 CDC Vouchers respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: These households have utilised $180 million, which is about 80% of the total vouchers available to them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Besides the CDC Vouchers, we have a mix of support measures given at the household and individual levels to help Singaporeans cope with inflation and cost of living concerns, with more help given to the lower-income and vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: This financial year, a low-income couple with two young children living in a 3-room HDB flat can expect to receive about $3,700 in various forms of support, such as cash, education top-ups, utilities and Service & Conservancy Charges (S&CC) rebates, and CDC Vouchers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The Government understands Singaporeans’ concerns over rising prices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We are carefully monitoring the situation and will consider if there is a need to provide more assistance, or bring forward some of the support schemes, especially if the situation worsens further.

sections.label: Targeted help for lower-income Singaporeans
sections.summary: The Government gives Edusave, Child Development Account top-ups, transport vouchers and GST-Voucher cash payments to eligible Singaporeans aged 21 and above, targeting lower-income groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We give Edusave and Child Development Account top-ups, and also public transport vouchers, just to name a few examples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We also provide additional GST-Voucher cash payments of up to $300 to eligible Singaporeans, aged 21 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, this is not household, this is to individuals, to eligible Singaporeans, aged 21 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: These are targeted to provide more assistance to lower-income Singaporeans, which, I think, is a better and more effective way compared to giving everybody $100 of CDC Vouchers, regardless of their wealth and income levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Because we know, given limited resources, it is correct to channel more funding to help our lower-income and vulnerable Singaporeans because they are more affected by rising prices.
